job.title: Business Development Director
job.description:
About the Opportunity


This is a Singapore-based, hybrid Business Development Director seat with a global investor services and fund administration firm with a long-established presence across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The APAC business is a meaningful engine for the wider group — the platform sells the full shelf: fund administration, corporate services, fiduciary, depositary, and regulatory solutions across PE, hedge, real assets, and credit strategies.


The seat reports directly into the Regional Chief Commercial Officer for APAC. You land into an established sales function with delivery and servicing teams already in place across Singapore and Hong Kong, and a mandate to drive new-logo growth in the Singapore market and across the wider region.


 

The Role

This is a hunter mandate. Day one looks like territory mapping, prospect lists, and getting the calendar full of business partner meetings — not waiting for marketing leads.


You will:

  • Own a defined APAC territory and a personal new-business pipeline across PE GPs, hedge fund managers, closed and open-ended fund managers, and selected corporate clients.
  • Run prospecting end-to-end — outbound, referral, market intelligence, and conference work — and translate that into qualified pipeline.
  • Lead RFPs and RFIs from discovery to signature, coordinating Operations, Tax, Legal, and the wider product specialist bench internally.
  • Maintain a steady cadence of business partner meetings and prospect wins each month, with a clear ramp expectation in the first six months and a step up thereafter.
  • Produce call reports, feed market intelligence back into the regional sales function, and build a current view of competitor activity across the APAC fund services landscape.
  • Represent the firm at industry events and stay close to regulatory and structuring trends across Singapore, Hong Kong, and offshore (Cayman, BVI).


The seat is sized for someone who has carried a number, not someone who has supported a process. If you are most proud of the pipeline you have personally built and the new logos you have personally landed, this seat is built around that profile.

 

What Makes You a Fit

You have probably spent 8 or more years in client-facing business development inside a fund administrator, asset servicer, or directly adjacent financial services platform — the kind of seat where a quarterly pipeline review is a real conversation, not a slide.


You have carried a quota, won new logos, and can talk through your last few wins with deal size, timeframe, and how the deal actually came together. You sell across PE, hedge, and closed/open-ended fund managers — and you are equally comfortable on a discovery call with a CFO at a mid-market PE shop and on a panel of stakeholders at a multi-strategy hedge fund.


You bring an active, warm APAC network — not "I know the market", but specific names you would call in week one. You have owned an RFP end-to-end, not just supported the bid team, and you can describe how you sequence Operations, Tax, and Legal inputs to hit a deadline.


You are Singapore-based (or able to land into a Singapore hybrid seat immediately), hold a relevant bachelor's degree, and you understand the APAC regulatory landscape — MAS at a minimum, with SFC, ASIC, and Cayman/BVI structuring in your peripheral vision.


The strongest fits will also bring some combination of:

  • A pedigreed seat at a recognised fund administrator or fund services platform.
  • Existing relationships with PE GPs, fund-of-funds, and family offices in the region.
  • Hedge and closed-end product fluency alongside private equity.
  • A track record of multi-year strategic accounts, not just one-shot wins.
  • Demonstrable RFP authoring and proposal-writing chops alongside the oral selling.

﻿

What is On Offer

  • A competitive base salary positioned at the senior end of the Singapore BDD market, plus an annual commission plan with meaningful new-logo and RFP-win economics on top.
  • A direct reporting line into the Regional Chief Commercial Officer, APAC — quick decisions, visible mandate, no layers between you and the people who set the strategy.
  • The full investor-services product shelf to sell, across all the major alternative asset classes — not a single-product ticket.
  • A hybrid working pattern out of a CBD office.
  • Comprehensive benefits, generous leave, private medical and life cover, and flexible working arrangements.
  • A platform with the brand and bench to back you on complex, multi-jurisdictional pitches.

job.title: Institutional BD Director
job.description:
The Opportunity


An established global investment solutions firm, with a dedicated asset management business, is building its Asia Pacific institutional distribution franchise from Singapore. This is the firm’s first dedicated asset management hire in the region — a hands-on, frontline sales role for someone who has already sold public markets investment products to institutional investors across APAC.


The platform has global scale, institutional backing, and established investment, product, portfolio management, marketing, legal, compliance, and RFP support across the US and Europe. The APAC mandate is product-led, with particular focus on long-only equity, factor-based equity, smart beta, systematic equity, and quantitative equity strategies.


Liquid alternatives and credit-related strategies are part of the broader platform, but the core priority for this hire is clear: open institutional doors and convert mandates for listed / liquid asset management products.

Singapore will be the regional base. The successful candidate will build the APAC client base from the ground up, starting from their own institutional relationships across Singapore, Korea, and broader APAC markets.


The Role


This is a frontline institutional business development role. It is not a team-management seat, regional figurehead role, or relationship-maintenance position.

You will be responsible for:

  • Originating and closing new institutional business across long-only equity, factor-based equity, smart beta, systematic equity, quantitative equity, and related listed / liquid asset management products
  • Building relationships with sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, insurers, investment consultants, central banks, private banks, and other institutional allocators across APAC
  • Leading the full sales cycle from initial engagement and investor education through due diligence, RFP / DDQ, and mandate award
  • Representing the firm credibly in front of CIOs, investment teams, consultants, and institutional decision-makers
  • Working with global product specialists, portfolio managers, marketing, legal, compliance, and RFP teams to support client discussions
  • Providing market intelligence on APAC investor appetite, competitor positioning, pricing, product demand, and distribution opportunities


You will report into senior asset management leadership overseas. You will have global support, but you will not inherit a local APAC book or local sales team. The expectation is that you can operate independently, build trust with institutional investors, and turn relationships into measurable AUM growth.


What Makes You a Fit

You will likely have:

  • Proven experience selling asset management products to institutional investors in APAC
  • Specific experience distributing long-only equity, factor-based equity, smart beta, systematic equity, or quantitative equity strategies
  • A track record of personally originating and closing institutional mandates, with clear examples of investor type, product sold, market covered, and AUM raised
  • Direct relationships across sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, insurers, investment consultants, central banks, private banks, or similar institutional allocators
  • Strong technical fluency in public markets investment products, including equity strategy positioning, factor exposures, portfolio construction, performance drivers, risk characteristics, and due diligence requirements
  • A hunter mindset and comfort building a market from scratch without relying on inherited accounts or a large local infrastructure
  • Singapore-based status or the ability to be based in Singapore quickly. Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency is preferred


It would be an advantage if you also have:

  • Experience selling liquid alternative products
  • Experience covering sovereign wealth funds or pension funds
  • ETF, index, or smart beta distribution experience
  • Korea, Japan, or broader North Asia institutional coverage
  • MAS Capital Markets Services Registered Representative status


What Is On Offer

  • A founding APAC institutional distribution seat within a global investment solutions platform with a dedicated asset management business
  • A product-led mandate focused on listed / liquid investment strategies with global investment and product support
  • The opportunity to build a regional franchise from Singapore
  • A performance-linked compensation structure designed to reward new business growth
  • Long-term potential to become the regional lead as the APAC business scales

job.title: AVP - FA Operation (Real Estate)
job.description:
AVP – Real Estate Fund Administration

Fund Administration | Real Assets / Alternative Investments | Singapore


The Opportunity


We are representing a global fund services platform supporting clients across alternative investments and real assets. As part of continued business growth, the firm is seeking an AVP – Real Estate Fund Administration to support a portfolio of real estate investment structures and oversee day-to-day fund administration activities.

This role combines fund accounting oversight, client servicing, stakeholder coordination, and team supervision within a regulated financial services environment.

The successful candidate will work closely with senior management while supervising a small team and acting as a key contact point for clients, investors, auditors, and other fund stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities


Fund Administration & Accounting Oversight

  • Support the administration of a portfolio of real estate and alternative investment funds in accordance with administration agreements and operational requirements
  • Maintain oversight of books and records, including review of Net Asset Value (NAV) calculations
  • Coordinate and review financial statements, periodic reports, and related performance reporting
  • Coordinate and review investor allocations relating to capital calls and distributions
  • Review capital account statements and related investor reporting documentation
  • Support payment processing activities and operational transaction flows


Client & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a primary day-to-day contact point for assigned clients and fund participants
  • Maintain professional relationships with investors, investment managers, banks, auditors, and other stakeholders
  • Work closely with Investor Relations teams to support investor communications and capital activity notices
  • Assist with client queries, service matters, and ongoing operational coordination


Team Leadership & Operational Support

  • Supervise and review work performed by junior team members
  • Provide guidance and support to team members on operational and reporting matters
  • Monitor deliverables to ensure service quality and compliance with agreed timelines
  • Assist with issue escalation and operational problem resolution where required


Projects & Process Improvement

  • Participate in internal projects and initiatives supporting operational improvement and business growth
  • Support presentations and discussions with existing or prospective clients where required
  • Monitor compliance with service agreements and operational procedures
  • Contribute to process enhancement initiatives across the business


Requirements


Experience

  • Minimum 4 years of experience within fund administration, accounting, asset management, or financial services environments
  • Prior exposure to real estate, real assets, or alternative investment fund structures
  • Experience supervising or guiding junior team members within a team environment


Education & Qualifications

  • Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related discipline
  • Professional accounting qualification (e.g. CA, CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) completed or in progress would be advantageous


Technical Skills

  • Working knowledge of IFRS and/or US GAAP
  • Experience reviewing general ledgers and financial statements
  • Familiarity with consolidation concepts and financial reporting processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
  • Experience using Yardi, MRI, or similar real estate / fund administration systems would be advantageous

﻿

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Organised and able to manage multiple deliverables and deadlines
  • Analytical and problem-solving capability
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team-based environment
  • Professional judgement and attention to detail

job.title: Executive Assistant - Private Equity Firm
job.description:
About the Opportunity


An established Singapore-based private equity firm is hiring an Executive Assistant to support select members of its investment team. This is a team EA seat — not a single-principal household PA role — and sits alongside the wider EA bench in a collegial, cover-each-other model.

The role reports into the Office Manager and works alongside a lean Singapore team based in the CBD. The seat is on-site and built for someone who wants ownership across a wider remit than a typical EA role: executive support, day-to-day office operations, and light IT and systems administration all sit under this hat.

This is a hire for someone who treats the office like their own — the kind of person an investment team comes to know and trust as the operational backbone of the firm.

 

The Role

You will provide secretariat support to select members of the investment team, alongside shared office operations and basic IT administration. The remit splits across three areas.


Executive support to the investment team

  • Calendar coordination, scheduling, and meeting logistics for the team members you support
  • Travel arrangements, including itineraries and last-minute changes as plans shift
  • Expense submissions and receipt reconciliation
  • Maintaining and updating contacts and address books
  • Occasional preparation of presentation materials and briefing notes


Office operations

  • Receiving visitors and preparing meeting rooms
  • Procurement and replenishment of office supplies
  • Liaising with building management on office maintenance, season parking, and facilities upkeep
  • Arranging courier and delivery services
  • Ad-hoc office administration, including BCP support and offsite planning


IT and systems administration

  • Basic troubleshooting for office equipment, printers, meeting room systems, and user access issues
  • Coordination with external IT vendors and service providers on installations, servicing, and replacements
  • IT setup support for new joiners
  • Maintaining inventory records of office IT equipment and assets
  • Maintaining IT documentation, user access records, and system subscriptions or licences


The seat is high-trust. You will handle confidential information across the team day in and day out, so discretion is non-negotiable.


What Makes You a Fit

You have spent at least five years in a true Executive Assistant capacity, ideally as a team EA supporting more than one executive in a fast-paced environment — private equity, asset management, family office, hedge fund, or boutique investment bank is a strong plus. You understand the rhythm of an investment team and can read when a calendar needs defending, when a flight needs rebooking before anyone has asked, and when to escalate.


You carry yourself well. Polished, articulate, and quietly confident — the kind of person who can engage external stakeholders at any level without ever drawing attention to yourself. You bring genuine energy and warmth to the team. This is not a heads-down back-office seat.


You are service-oriented by instinct. You take ownership of problems rather than passing them on, and you are comfortable wearing more than one hat. You know that in a smaller team, the line between EA work, office work, and IT work is artificial — and you are happy to step across it.


You read a room well and work with the grain of an established team. This is a settled, collegial group with its own way of doing things, so you bring your ideas and improvements quietly and collaboratively rather than looking to overhaul from day one. You are calm under pressure, low-ego, and happy to be the dependable presence behind the scenes.


You are technologically comfortable. You can troubleshoot the everyday issues that come up in a modern office, you pick up new tools quickly, and you are happy to be the go-to person for the team on anything from a stuck printer to a calendar sync issue.


You hold the right to work in Singapore.


Bonus points if:

  • You have prior experience supporting investment professionals at a PE firm, asset manager, family office, or hedge fund
  • You come from a financial services, family office, or fund-operations background and bring strong EA or admin aptitude
  • You are familiar with Concur for expense management and SAP
  • You have coordinated with external IT vendors on procurement and account management
  • You have run business continuity or offsite working setups
  • You hold a degree from a recognised institution
  • You speak Mandarin in addition to English


What is On Offer

  • Competitive base salary with a meaningful discretionary bonus structure
  • Full-time, on-site role in a well-located CBD office
  • A seat close to a respected investment team, with broad exposure across the operational picture of a private equity firm
  • A small, professional, low-drama environment where good work is noticed

job.title: Fund Accounting Manager
job.description:
Fund Accounting Manager — Private Capital & Hedge Funds

Singapore | Full-time | Fund Administration

We are representing a boutique, independent fund administration and corporate services firm with an international office network, as it continues to grow its Fund Services team in Singapore. They are looking for a Fund Accounting Manager to take ownership of a portfolio of Private Equity, Venture Capital, Real Estate and Hedge Fund structures and SPVs.

This is a hands-on, client-facing role with a high degree of autonomy. You will be the main point of contact for your clients, own the financial, operational and client service results of your portfolio, and help improve the processes and systems behind the Singapore office's growth. It suits a fund accountant who wants broad, multi-strategy exposure and direct contact with clients and boards, in a firm where everyone's work counts.

What you will own

Portfolio and clients

  • Manage a portfolio of fund and SPV clients across Private Equity, Venture Capital, Real Estate and Hedge Fund structures, as the main contact for fund managers, investors, banks, auditors and legal advisers.
  • Lead and support client meetings with accurate data and proactive follow-up.
  • Where required, hold fund or SPV directorships and take part in board meetings, presenting and explaining financial accounts and fund reports.

Fund accounting and reporting

  • Prepare and review fund and SPV accounts: NAV calculations, capital accounts, management and performance fees, investor allocations, cash reconciliations and expense accruals.
  • Prepare and review statutory annual financial statements under US GAAP, IFRS and SFRS, and run the audit with external auditors through to completion.
  • Review investor communications, including capital call and distribution notices and investor statements.

Payments, tax and investor services

  • Oversee bank accounts and the execution of authorised client payments.
  • Prepare and review GST and tax filings with external tax advisers, including GST remission scheme applications where applicable.
  • Oversee and guide transfer agency work: investor onboarding and KYC/AML reviews, subscriptions and redemptions, investor registers, and FATCA and CRS reporting.

Team and improvement

  • Identify and put in place process, workflow and system improvements that make the Fund Services team more efficient, scalable and controlled.
  • Guide junior colleagues on transfer agency and compliance matters, and share technical knowledge with colleagues across the firm's global offices.

What you will bring

  • A bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related field.
  • At least 7 years of fund accounting experience with a fund administrator or in an equivalent setting, including independently managing a portfolio of fund clients.
  • Solid fund accounting knowledge across private capital and hedge fund structures: NAV computation, capital account maintenance and financial statements under US GAAP, IFRS and SFRS.
  • Working knowledge of AML, investor due diligence, FATCA and CRS reporting, and familiarity with Singapore regulatory requirements for fund structures.
  • Fluent written and spoken English, as the role works daily with clients, auditors, banks and advisers; strong client relationship skills.
  • A track record of managing several client relationships and deadlines at once, working closely within a small team.

Advantageous

  • Experience with fund accounting systems such as Paxus or FIS Private Capital Suite.

Why consider this role

  • Ownership of a multi-asset-class book — PE, VC, Real Estate and Hedge Funds — rather than a single strategy.
  • Direct exposure to fund managers, investors and boards, including directorship mandates.
  • A boutique firm with an informal culture and an international network, where your work contributes directly to the business.
  • Room to shape processes and systems as the Singapore office grows.

Interested?

Apply through this posting, or message Hui Shuen Lim at FP GLOBAL for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Senior Fund Accountant
job.description:
Senior Fund Accountant — Hedge Funds | Singapore

The Opportunity

We are representing a boutique fund administration and corporate services firm in Singapore. Its Fund Services team is lean and looks after a portfolio of fund and SPV structures, with a particular focus on hedge funds and other open-ended funds, and exposure to private equity, venture capital and real estate structures.

Our client is seeking a Senior Fund Accountant to deepen the Singapore office's hedge fund accounting capability. The role owns the day-to-day deliverables of a client portfolio as first point of contact for clients, and acts as a technical reference point for colleagues on hedge fund and derivative accounting.

In a lean team, the role covers the full cycle: NAV production, reconciliations, valuation, financial statements, audit and transfer agency work, with direct contact with fund managers, investors, prime brokers, custodians and banks.

The Role

  • Based in Singapore
  • Reports to the Fund Accounting Managers
  • Works with the firm's centre of excellence and global offices

Key Responsibilities

Client portfolio

  • Manage a portfolio of fund and SPV clients, predominantly hedge fund and open-ended fund structures, together with private equity, venture capital and real estate structures
  • Act as first point of contact for clients, prime brokers and other external stakeholders, escalating complex matters to the Fund Accounting Managers where appropriate

Hedge fund accounting and valuation

  • Prepare NAVs for hedge funds and other open-ended funds, including trade capture, corporate actions, pricing and valuation, accruals, P&L analysis, and management and performance fee calculations (high-water marks, hurdles, crystallisation, equalisation and series accounting)
  • Account for and value equities, fixed income, FX and digital assets, including exchange-traded and OTC derivatives (interest rate swaps, total return swaps, credit default swaps, equity and CFD swaps, futures, forwards and options), and process trade lifecycle events
  • Perform daily and periodic reconciliations of cash, positions, trades, margin and collateral against prime broker, custodian, clearing broker and ISDA counterparty records
  • Review and challenge derivative and hard-to-value pricing, including independent price verification, and support Level 1, 2 and 3 fair value hierarchy classification

Private markets

  • Prepare private equity, venture capital, real estate fund and SPV accounts, including capital accounts, capital calls and distributions, waterfalls and carried interest

Financial statements and audit

  • Prepare statutory annual financial statements under US GAAP, IFRS and SFRS, including financial instrument, derivative and fair value disclosures
  • Manage the audit process with external auditors

Transfer agency, payments and tax

  • Investor onboarding and KYC/AML reviews; subscription, redemption, switch and transfer processing; investor register maintenance; FATCA and CRS reporting
  • Prepare investor communications, including NAV and performance statements, contract notes, capital call and distribution notices
  • Prepare and execute authorised client payments and, with external tax advisers, GST and tax compliance filings

Team and improvement

  • Mentor junior fund accountants and review their work
  • Support new client onboarding, fund launches, process and system improvements, and prospective client discussions

Candidate Profile

Essential

  • Bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or an equivalent field
  • At least 3–5 years of fund accounting experience in a fund administrator, hedge fund or equivalent, a substantial portion in hedge fund accounting, including managing a portfolio of fund clients
  • Hands-on hedge fund accounting: daily and monthly NAV production, trade and position reconciliations, multi-currency and multi-asset portfolios, short positions and financing, and performance fee methodologies (equalisation, series accounting, high-water marks)
  • Financial statement preparation under US GAAP, IFRS and SFRS
  • Familiarity with derivatives: trade lifecycle, valuation inputs, margin and collateral, and accounting and disclosure treatment (ASC 820 / IFRS 13, ASC 815 / IFRS 7 and IFRS 9)
  • Working knowledge of AML, investor due diligence, and FATCA and CRS reporting for transfer agency activities
  • Familiarity with Singapore regulatory requirements applicable to fund structures
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills
  • Fluent English, as the role is the first point of contact for clients, investors and counterparties

Advantageous

  • Professional accounting qualification (e.g. CA, CPA or ACCA), completed or in progress
  • Working knowledge of prime brokerage arrangements and ISDA/CSA documentation
  • Private equity, venture capital or real estate fund accounting (capital accounts, capital calls and distributions, waterfalls)
  • Experience with Paxus or FIS Private Capital Suite
  • Experience with CRS, GST remission and tax filings

Why Consider This Role?

  • End-to-end ownership of a client portfolio in a lean team
  • Technical depth across hedge fund, derivative and private markets accounting
  • A technical reference role for colleagues, including mentoring junior fund accountants

Application Process

To apply, please submit your CV through this page, quoting job reference 132016.

Fair Hiring Statement

FP GLOBAL is committed to fair employment practices. All applications are assessed on merit against job-related criteria, regardless of age, race, gender, religion, marital status, family responsibilities or disability.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
We are supporting a large Asia-Pacific alternative investment manager as it hires a Finance Manager in Singapore to own the finance, governance and compliance of its SPV and holding-entity platform.

The firm holds its investments through SPVs across several jurisdictions. This role is the single owner of their accounts, audits, tax and statutory filings and governance. It also coordinates the external accountants, corporate-secretarial firms, tax advisors, auditors and legal counsel who support the platform.

What you will do

  • Review SPV financial statements and management accounts, and set accounting treatments for investments, shareholder funding, redeemable preference shares, intercompany balances and distributions
  • Manage SPV statutory audits, annual declarations, tax computations and filings, including India advance tax
  • Own the SPV governance framework: policies, workflows, manuals and responsibility matrices
  • Run Singapore board meetings, resolutions, share issuances and statutory registers
  • Oversee SPV treasury across jurisdictions and monitor every key deadline
  • Act as the central coordination point for external service providers, and improve processes and controls
  • Support projects and restructurings

What you will bring

  • Hands-on experience with Singapore entities: financial statements, statutory audits, and corporate-secretarial or tax filings
  • Typically 7–12 years across private funds, alternatives, fund finance, SPV accounting, governance, tax compliance, corporate services or professional services
  • Strong SPV financial statement review under IFRS / SG GAAP; CPA, CA or ACCA preferred
  • Familiarity with master-feeder and parallel funds, shareholder loans, redeemable preference shares, holding structures and 13O / 13U schemes is an advantage
  • Experience managing external accountants, corporate-secretarial firms, tax advisors and auditors
  • Advanced Excel; Power BI and AI tools are a plus
  • Clear English communication, careful planning across many entities, and a strong sense of ownership

Why this role: you will own a whole SPV platform on the buy side, covering accounting, audit, tax, corporate secretarial and treasury, and design the governance framework as well as run it.

The role is based in Singapore. To apply or have a confidential conversation, contact Diana Teh at FP GLOBAL.

job.title: Regional Business Development Manager
job.description:
Regional Business Development Manager

We exist to re-engineer nature’s pantry: fish-free omega-3, straight from algae, for food, beverage, infant nutrition, and animal nutrition. This role turns that science into trusted regional supply. You will open and grow accounts that need a sustainable, high-quality source of essential nutrition, and you will make the path from first conversation to commercial use clear, credible, and worth repeating.

Performance Objectives

  • Build a qualified regional pipeline and convert it into agreed revenue, volume, and margin for algal omega-3 oils.
  • Move priority accounts from sampling and application trials to approved, repeat supply, coordinating technical, quality, and regulatory support.
  • Establish the right mix of direct customers and distribution so coverage, service, and economics improve together.
  • Structure pricing and commercial terms that hold value against fish oil and other algal alternatives.
  • Deliver a rolling demand forecast accurate enough for supply planning, and flag risks early.
  • Bring customer application needs and competitive insight back into product and portfolio decisions.
  • Create qualified opportunities through customer forums and selected industry events, then follow them to a decision.

Environment & Resources

You report to regional commercial leadership and work as a senior individual contributor with global product management, applications, regulatory, quality, and supply chain. You will have pricing guidance, samples, technical collateral, and a CRM to run the pipeline. Expect regular travel across the region and close work with customers who formulate, trial, and qualify ingredients before they buy.

Essential Qualifications

  • Seven or more years in business development or technical sales of nutritional, food, or specialty ingredients.
  • A record of taking B2B accounts through specification, claims, trials, and supplier qualification to supply.
  • An active network among food, beverage, infant nutrition, or supplement manufacturers in the region.
  • Comfort with contribution margin, pricing structures, and volume forecasts.
  • Ability to explain algal-oil performance in the language of formulators and buyers.
  • Fluency in English; another regional business language is an advantage.

Role Selling Points

  • A science-led portfolio with a clear point of difference: omega-3 from algae, not fish.
  • Influence on how products are positioned, priced, and launched, not only how they are sold.
  • Work that connects commercial results to a more sustainable nutrition system.
  • Competitive pay and benefits, plus support for health and wellbeing.
  • A team that values diversity and will accommodate access needs.

Call to Action

Apply with a brief note on one regional ingredient win you led from first meeting to supply. Show us the outcome, the obstacles, and what you would do differently here.
job.salary: SGD 8,000 - 10,000 per month base, plus performance bonus (see notes)

job.title: SVP - Funds of Funds (Fund Accounting)
job.description:
SVP, Funds of Funds – Fund Accounting | Singapore

We are supporting a leading global fund administrator in appointing a Senior Vice President to lead its Funds of Funds fund accounting team in Singapore. Fund administration is the firm's core business, and this is a senior leadership role with ownership of technical delivery, people, key clients and operational risk.

  • Leadership and development of a team of AVPs and Senior Account Managers: coaching, performance management and succession.

Why consider it

  • A senior seat in a business where fund administration is the core, not a side line.
  • Breadth across technical accounting, people leadership, client delivery and risk.

The role is based in Singapore.

For a confidential conversation, contact Diana Teh at Funds Partnership (diana@fundspartnership.com).

job.title: Senior Vice President / Executive Director - Operations
job.description:
Senior Vice President / Executive Director, Operations — Singapore


A well-established alternative investment manager with a sizeable Asia platform is expanding its team in Singapore, as the firm and its range of products have grown. This seat covers operations across three connected areas: fund operations, firm operations and portfolio operations.


You will be the operations person on the ground in Singapore, working closely with colleagues across the region. The seat sits close to firm leadership and reports to a senior partner who covers the region and spends time in Singapore, so the work runs on your own judgement, with clear updates and regular check-ins rather than day-to-day supervision.


The firm moves quickly and priorities can shift. The seat suits someone who keeps things moving and makes sure deadlines are met. Occasional regional travel is part of the job.


This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor seat, with no team to manage, and that is by design. You will do well here if you have spent a meaningful part of your career inside a fund manager (GP), not only advising or servicing one. Experience with USD funds or global fund structures is valued, as the funds grow more complex. Private equity is the most natural fit, though GP experience in private credit, real estate, infrastructure or public markets counts just as much. People who have worked with you would describe you as technical, reliable, hardworking and low-ego.


A separate senior finance seat for the management company is also open. If your background has historically covered both operations and finance, we would like to hear from you too.


On offer: a senior seat close to firm leadership at a well-regarded investment platform and a competitive package calibrated to experience. Notice periods are respected — the firm would rather wait for the right person.

job.title: Assistant Vice President - Private Credit
job.description:
Assistant Vice President – Private Credit Fund Accounting
Singapore | Permanent

We are supporting a global fund administrator in hiring an Assistant Vice President for its Private Credit team in Singapore. This is a newly created role, opened as the team expands.

You will take ownership of a portfolio of private credit funds, working alongside the Vice President and reviewing the work of a small team of accountants. You will also be the day-to-day contact for the clients you look after.

The team welcomes candidates from private equity fund accounting as well as private credit. If your background is in closed-ended PE funds and you want to build private credit expertise, we would like to hear from you.

What you'll do

Fund accounting and reporting

  • Maintain books and records and calculate fund NAVs for a portfolio of private credit funds.
  • Coordinate and review financial statements and monthly or quarterly reporting, including performance metrics.
  • Review carried interest, performance and incentive fee calculations.

Investor and capital activity

  • Review capital calls, distributions and equalisations, including investor allocations.
  • Review partner capital account statements and coordinate payments and other transactions.
  • Work with the Investor Relations team on investor queries and capital activity notices.

Clients and stakeholders

  • Act as the primary day-to-day contact for clients and other fund participants, including investment managers, banks and auditors.
  • Support the audit process and monitor service level agreements and other client agreements.
  • Take part in presentations to existing and prospective clients.

Team

  • Supervise junior accountants, reviewing and signing off their work.
  • Contribute to projects as the business grows.

What you'll bring

Essential

  • CA, CPA, ACCA or an equivalent professional qualification.
  • 6+ years' accounting experience in financial services, ideally in private credit, private equity, asset management or fund administration.
  • Experience in limited partnership (closed-ended fund) accounting.
  • Experience preparing and reviewing general ledgers and financial statements under IFRS and/or US GAAP, including consolidation under IFRS.
  • 3–4 years' experience supervising or leading staff.
  • Clear written and spoken English, as the role involves regular reporting to and communication with clients, investors and auditors.

Preferred

  • Working knowledge of Investran, or another private equity or private credit system such as eFront.
  • Private equity or private credit fund administration experience.
  • Strong command of Excel and enterprise accounting systems.

Why consider this role?

  • It's a newly created role in an expanding team, not a backfill.
  • You'll own a portfolio of funds and supervise a team at AVP level.
  • It's a route into private credit for experienced PE fund accountants.
  • Our client offers training and education support and flexible working arrangements.

job.title: Manager Company Secretarial Services
job.description:
About the Opportunity


An established international corporate and fiduciary services group is investing in senior corporate secretarial coverage in its boutique Singapore office, and the client base here is growing.


This is a rare seat with real ownership. You would act as company secretary for a portfolio of client companies. You would set up the entity database, the compliance calendar and the procedures, and shape how the desk runs as the office grows. It comes with direct access to the Managing Director, not a maintenance seat inside an established department.


The Role

You would own the corporate secretarial function end to end for a portfolio of Singapore private limited companies



Responsibilities

 

A. Corporate Secretarial Services for Clients

  • Manage a portfolio of client companies incorporated in Singapore and overseas.
  • Serve as named Company Secretary for client entities where appointed.
  • Ensure compliance with the Singapore Companies Act and ACRA requirements.
  • Prepare and maintain statutory registers, minute books, and corporate records.
  • Draft and lodge corporate filings with ACRA.
  • Organize and support: incorporations, Annual General Meetings (where applicable), Directors' and shareholders' resolutions, share allotments and transfers, Changes in officers, Amendments to company constitutions, Business cessation and striking-off applications and other professional activities as requested by the Company.
  • Advise clients on routine corporate governance and statutory compliance matters.
  • Monitor statutory deadlines and ensure timely filing obligations are met.
  • Liaise with clients, regulators, auditors, banks, tax agents, and other external stakeholders.

 

B. Internal Corporate Secretarial Responsibilities

  • Act as Company Secretary for the firm.
  • Maintain internal statutory records and registers.
  • Coordinate board meetings and prepare meeting agendas, notices, minutes, and resolutions.
  • Ensure the company's own corporate filings and compliance obligations are completed accurately and on time.
  • Support management in implementing corporate governance policies and best practices.

 

 

C. Registered Qualified Individual (RQI) Responsibilities

  • Act as the Registered Qualified Individual under applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure corporate secretarial services are delivered in accordance with Singapore legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain oversight of client acceptance, ongoing administration, and service standards.
  • Review and approve company incorporations and significant corporate actions where required.
  • Ensure proper maintenance of client records and statutory documentation.
  • Support regulatory inspections, audits, and information requests.
  • Provide technical guidance and training to corporate secretarial staff.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and implement necessary procedural updates.

 

D. Local Directorship (for the Singapore company ONLY)

  • Act as the local Resident Director for the Company

 

E. KYC, AML/CFT and Client Onboarding Compliance

  • Lead and manage all client onboarding processes.
  • Conduct Know-Your-Customer (KYC), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) reviews.
  • Review and verify: identification documents; corporate ownership structures; Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs); source of funds/source of wealth information; sanctions screening results; Politically Exposed Person (PEP) checks; adverse media screening outcomes; Assess and document customer risk ratings
  • Make recommendations regarding acceptance or rejection of prospective clients.
  • Maintain complete onboarding and compliance records.
  • Perform periodic customer reviews and ongoing monitoring.
  • Escalate suspicious or high-risk matters to management and the firm's Compliance Officer where appropriate.
  • Support AML/CFT audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory inspections.
  • Develop and update internal KYC and onboarding procedures.

job.title: Research Assistant (Japan Equities)
job.description:
Japanese Equities Research Assistant/ Analyst (Buy-Side)

Location: Singapore

Representing: Leading Japan-Focused Investment Manager

Language Requirement: Business-level Japanese (JLPT N1 or above) and fluent English

 

About the Opportunity

We are partnering with a leading Japan-focused investment management firm renowned for its deep fundamental research and disciplined long-term approach to equity investing.

The team manages concentrated, high-conviction portfolios across mid to small-cap Japanese companies, identifying underappreciated value through on-the-ground insights, management engagement, and rigorous bottom-up analysis.

This opportunity is ideal for an analytically sharp, bilingual professional who wants to immerse themselves in the Japanese equity markets, develop direct relationships with company management teams, and contribute to active investment decisions within a buy-side environment.

 

The Role

As a Research Assistant, you will work directly with Portfolio Managers and Senior Analysts across the full investment process — from idea generation and financial modelling to valuation, monitoring, and thesis refinement.

While the title is “Assistant”, this role operates within a lean team structure and carries responsibilities typically associated with an Analyst / Associate-level position. You will be expected to take ownership of research outputs and contribute actively to investment discussions rather than provide purely administrative support.

 

This is a highly visible role within a flat and collaborative investment culture, offering a strong platform to develop sector expertise and grow into a decision-making position over time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct in-depth fundamental research on listed Japanese companies across assigned sectors (e.g., Industrials, Consumer, Technology).
  • Build and maintain detailed financial models to assess earnings drivers, valuation, and business fundamentals.
  • Perform company due diligence, including attending management meetings, industry conferences, and site visits.
  • Monitor macroeconomic, industry, and policy developments that impact Japanese equities.
  • Prepare investment theses, presentations, and reports for internal investment committees.
  • Collaborate closely with the trading and operations teams to support efficient portfolio execution and monitoring.
  • Contribute to periodic investor updates and performance analyses, as needed.

Who We’re Looking For

  • Experience: 1–4 years in equity research, investment banking, consulting, or a related analytical field. Candidates with relevant internships or strong academic backgrounds will also be considered.
  • Language: Native or business-level Japanese (JLPT N1); strong English communication skills required.
  • Education: Degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a quantitative discipline.
  • Skills: Strong financial modelling, valuation, and analytical skills. Familiarity with Bloomberg, FactSet, or similar research tools is advantageous.
  • Traits: Intellectually curious, detail-oriented, and self-driven with a genuine passion for understanding businesses and markets.

Why This Role

  • Work directly with portfolio managers and decision-makers in a true buy-side environment.
  • Gain exposure to cross-sector Japanese equities and direct access to management teams.
  • Join a flat, meritocratic culture that values research depth and independent thinking.
  • Build a long-term career path with mentorship and progressive responsibility.

How to Apply

We are exclusively representing this search.

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity and insights into the firm’s culture and investment philosophy, please reach out to us directly.
